title: Enumeration - content ids (category << 12 | index) used by chests, loot, shops and rewards

container.notes: Enumeration spec: no file of its own. The pseudo-record describes how an id stored in a u16 field of other formats splits into bit fields; the enums give the labels.

records.name: contentId
records.count: one per field that holds a content id
records.where: Chest item fields (treasure-chests), unit loot fields (foe-drops, ard-units), shop, bazaar, reward and package tables of the battlepack.

bits.name: index
bits.notes: Index in the category (gil amount for category 14).

ContentCategory.1: Equipment (weapons 0x1000-0x10C7, armour 0x10C8-0x1153, accessories 0x1154-0x1183, ammunition 0x1184-0x11A3, foe-only weapons and gear 0x11A4-0x122C)
ContentCategory.8: Key item (0x8000-0x81FF; maps, monographs 0x8069.., Canopic Jar 0x806C)

roundTrip: Store as a plain u16; 0xFFFF means nothing.
Gil inside a content id is limited to 4095 (0xE000-0xEFFF); chest gil fields are plain amounts and are not content ids.
Use only ids that exist in the target table (Reserve labels mark unused rows).
gaps: Conflict: TK L1590 states gil = 0xF000 | amount, but the same Toolkit list ends at 61439 = 0xEFFF "4095 Gil" (TK L1574) and vanilla ARD data uses 57844 = 0xE1F4 for 500 gil (GS:ARDMap 4: Units!AM); this spec follows the data (0xE000).
The Drops sheet labels 0xE1F4 "Reserve" (its own lookup), so its names for gil ids are not reliable.
